messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: sev2 - routing errors + high 5xx rate observed for eu-west cluster affecting model routing. Pager: @sanjay on-call. Links: https://ops.redwood/alerts/1773456789 :rotating_light:
sanjay: acked, looking now. seeing 502 spikes from eu-west -> backend returns 'model_not_found' for a subset of requests. this looks like wrong model variant being routed. I’m checking routing policy logs and DNS endpoints for eu-west edge nodes.
kevin: any customer reports?
lisa (CS): one paying customer (Acme Apps) reported elevated errors around 14:02 UTC, narrow spike. CS escalation raised.
sanjay: root cause hypothesis: smart-routing fallback policy tried eu-west-primary -> eu-west-secondary but some edge endpoints still resolving to old/removed hosts (stale DNS). fallback loop toggling model variant between v1-small and v2-quantized leading to incompatible model mapping -> model_not_found.
maria: how do we confirm DNS staleness? can we NSLOOKUP / curl the edge IPs from a couple of regions?
tony (eng-sre): I can run checks from GCE, AWS, and our monitoring probes. running: ``dig +short edge-eu-west.redwood.net`` and ``curl -sI https://edge-eu-west.redwood.net/ping``
kevin: meanwhile, can we short-circuit smart-routing for this customer to avoid bad variants?
sanjay: yes. temporary mitigation: pin routing policy for affected customers to 'eu-global-stable' (no region fallback) and disable automatic model variant fallback. executing canary rollback now.
(tony runs): tony (eng-sre): ip dig results show mixed A records: two healthy hosts + one stale host (old IP) still in DNS. TTL for record is 300s but looks like a cached value at some resolvers.
(incident-bot): deploy-bot: policy-change applied by sanjay at 14:08 UTC: pinned route for tenant=acme to eu-global-stable.
sanjay: pinned and testing. generating synthetic requests -> errors drop to baseline. good.
lisa (CS): confirming with Acme: they see errors go away. thanks.
kevin: what about other tenants? is this limited or wider?
maria: monitoring shows a small set of tenants routed through that edge pool. we'll push pinned policy for them as a precaution and monitor.
tony (eng-sre): contacting DNS provider (dns-support) to request cache flush and check propagation. message sent: "we see stale A record for edge-eu-west, may be stuck in our provider's cache"
dns-support: ack. provider reports they cleared their cache at 14:12 UTC, but some public resolvers (ISP-level) may continue to serve cached results until TTL expiry. advising to lower TTL for impacted records.
sanjay: immediate plan: 1) keep routing pinned (no auto-fallback) 2) increase observability on route-level error counts and model mapping mismatches 3) CS outreach to notify customers of transient impact 4) schedule postmortem and change to routing policy defaults.
kevin: do we need to rotate keys or change anything else? sounds config-only.
maria: config-only. we should proactively reduce TTL on edge records to 60s for the next 24h to speed propagation for future changes. make change and then revert.
(incident-bot): incident-bot: severity escalated to SEV1 potential if propagation persists beyond 30m. current status: contained.
sanjay: adding runbook note: runbook/inbound-routing#dns-fallback-loop - include step to pin policy and disable fallback.
kevin: who owns postmortem? sanjay or tony?
sanjay: I'll lead the postmortem with tony and maria. lisa please coordinate customer communications and attach logs.
lisa (CS): will prepare customer summary and work through refunds/credits if needed.
tony (eng-sre): follow-ups: 1) change default fallback threshold on smart-router to avoid variant oscillation on partial DNS failures, 2) add an automated check that validates model variant existence before rerouting, 3) TTL change plan and docs for ops.
maria: also recommend adding a per-route circuit breaker that blocks variant swap if more than X% of nodes return model_not_found.
sanjay: agreed. I'll open the rollout PR for fallback-threshold and variant-existence check. linking: https://github.com/redwood-inference/smart-router/pull/412
(incident-bot): incident-bot: incident declared resolved at 14:24 UTC after pinned routing stabilized and provider cache cleared. monitoring will remain on high-sensitivity for next 2 hours.
kevin: thanks team. quick timeline and notes for postmortem: root cause = mix of DNS stale endpoints + aggressive fallback policy creating oscillation and wrong model variant routing. customer impact limited but visible to a few tenants.
sanjay: filing incident ticket and timeline. will add logs and config diffs.
lisa (CS): I'll follow-up with Acme and inform them we're doing a postmortem and will share findings.
kevin: good job. small action items assigned. close after postmortem and TTL change. :thumbsup:
